narrativeProgression.description: Jon introduces himself and his unique experience of having 'a thousand voices' due to relying on interpreters.
He highlights the inconsistency of vocal representation for individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing.
He shares a humorous anecdote about how the tone of his interpreters sometimes doesn't match his own energetic personality.
Jon presents a call to action, urging viewers to get involved in revolutionizing AI for genuine inclusivity in communication.

youtube_description:
Jon Mowl, founder of Play with ASL relies on a variety of interpreters to serve as his “voice.” But what if there were a way to personalize communication for people with disabilities, to give them a voice that matched their desired tone, personality, energy and feelings?

At #HackDisability: AI for Accessibility, teams of innovators will come together to address known challenges facing the disability community, including AI for communication. 

💡 Are you up for the challenge? If so, we want you hacking alongside us, building a more accessible world. Register today: Perkins.org/HackDisability
